headline_marked: [[Google Maps]] satellite view drains phone battery; here's how to fix it
headline: Google Maps satellite view drains phone battery; here's how to fix it
summary: A simple toggle in Google Maps settings can significantly improve your phone's battery life when navigating outdoors, especially during extended use like hiking.
details: For avid hikers and outdoor explorers, keeping Google Maps open for navigation can be a major battery drain. A hidden setting, the satellite view, consumes more power than standard map views due to increased screen rendering and constant location updates.

The solution is straightforward: disable the 'Start maps in Satellite View' option within the app's settings. This change ensures Google Maps defaults to a more battery-efficient standard map view, preserving your phone's power for longer periods.

While satellite view offers detailed imagery, standard maps provide essential information like roads, compass orientation, and mapped features. For topographical data, the terrain view is a more efficient alternative to satellite imagery.

Disabling satellite view won't magically double your battery life, as GPS and display usage are primary power consumers. However, the cumulative effect of reducing unnecessary rendering in satellite mode can add up, especially during all-day excursions.

In situations where precise visual detail is crucial, such as identifying unclear trail junctions or navigating poorly marked paths, satellite view can still be manually activated by tapping the layers button.

headline: Apple lays off 200+ staffers across Vision Pro and Siri teams
summary: The tech giant is reportedly making significant cuts to its spatial computing and AI assistant divisions, impacting over 200 employees.
details: Apple has laid off more than 200 employees, primarily impacting teams working on the Vision Pro headset and the Siri voice assistant. The cuts reportedly include the "largely shutting down" of a Vision Pro gaming team and a reduction in the size of the immersive content team for the device.

This move comes as the $3,499 Vision Pro headset, launched in early 2024, has not seen widespread adoption. Despite ongoing development for a successor, Apple has also reportedly paused work on an entry-level XR device display.

In contrast, Apple recently unveiled its revamped, AI-powered Siri at WWDC, with a public beta expected later this year. The company stated the changes are to "evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users," while also creating new roles.

The company is also reportedly planning to enter the smart glasses market, with announcements anticipated around WWDC 2027 and a launch by the end of that year, following the success of similar products from competitors like Meta.
